name: Motorized Bicycle
description: Minnesota's moped: a bicycle-style vehicle propelled by an electric or liquid-fuel motor of no more than two brake horsepower (1,492 W) that can't go faster than 30 mph on a flat surface; pedals aren't required. An electric two-wheeler outside the electric-assisted bicycle limits lands here while it stays within these. Defined by Minnesota Statutes §169.011, subd. 45, and regulated by §169.223.
restrictions: Propelled by an electric or liquid-fuel motor of no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,492 W); a fuel engine is also capped at 50 cc
Can't go faster than 30 mph on a flat surface with the motor engaged
Pedals aren't required: the definition calls it a bicycle, but it can be fully self-propelled
Faster or more powerful than this, a two- or three-wheeler is a motorcycle, the default category for them
Riders need a driver's license, a motorized bicycle operator's permit or a motorized bicycle instruction permit; permits are available from age 15 and no motorcycle endorsement is needed
An instruction permit holder may ride only within one mile of home
Riders under 18 must wear a helmet, and a bicycle helmet meeting 16 CFR part 1203 qualifies; every rider must wear eye protection
Titled and registered with a rear license plate, and must carry liability insurance
A new one sold in Minnesota must have a headlight, which must be on whenever it's ridden
Ridden as close as practicable to the right-hand edge of the roadway
Not allowed on sidewalks except to reach the roadway, or on bike paths or bike lanes reserved for nonmotorized traffic
